axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself; it is an interface implementation called by clients.
It gives agents **version-aware library and API documentation**,
solving usage errors caused by stale model training data.
axes.local_files: **No local file access at all.** A pure documentation-retrieval service.
axes.background:
**Always available as a remotely hosted service**, independent of the client process lifecycle —
the only entry in this section unaffected by your machine's switch.

But **service availability depends on Upstash's service status**;
this repository's releases cannot guarantee the server side — the two must be judged separately.
axes.tools:
It provides MCP tools for retrieving library documentation.

The README stresses correct usage: use Library Ids, **specify a version** ("Specify a Version"),
and declare via a rule that Context7 should always be used when library docs are needed.
Output is structured documentation content.
axes.context:
No cross-session memory, but **documentation retrieval is itself "external memory"** —
compensating for stale model training data; that is its core positioning.
axes.permissions:
**The permission risk profile is completely different from local servers**:
it touches no local files, but **your query content is sent to Upstash servers**.

Passing a Library Id and a question produces a network request.
Authentication uses an API key (`Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`).
There is no separate approval mechanism.
axes.fit:
Scenarios where you need current-version library docs: API changes after a library upgrade,
config options introduced by new versions, third-party library usage the model is unsure about.
Not a fit for internal code or private libraries.

mcp.transport:
**Remote Streamable HTTP**, server endpoint `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`.

**The only entry in this section whose default form is a remote service** —
all other official reference servers are local stdio processes.
mcp.auth:
**An API key is required**, passed via the `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` header.
The README says installers can generate the key automatically through an OAuth flow.

**Quota tiers verified (rolling re-check 2026-10-23, official plans page)**:
Free **1,000 calls/month** (Search API + Context API combined),

Pro **2,000 calls/seat/month**, overage **does not block** (overage unit price not stored per our D9 rule; see the official plans page).

Also, the Free tier itself already uses OAuth 2.0 (the official comparison table lists OAuth 2.0 under Free).
⚠ **The exact behaviour after Free exceeds its quota: the official page gives no answer body**, only the question title.
mcp.scope:
**No local permission risk, but there is a data-egress risk**:
query content is sent to Upstash servers.
The library names and question text you pass are outbound content;
sensitive scenarios need an assessment.

**This round adds one explicit official privacy commitment** (the official FAQ title is
"How do you keep the privacy of my queries?"):

Queries send only **the documentation question and the library name/ID**,
not full prompts, source code or conversation history;
and the official docs require agents not to include credentials, personal data or proprietary code in queries.

The document-index scope on the server side is Upstash's; it is not visible to clients.

sections.为什么它和其他条目不一样:
| Dimension | Other reference servers | Context7 |
|---|---|---|
| Run form | Local process (stdio) | **Remote HTTP service** |
| Data flow | Stays on your machine | **Queries go to Upstash** |
| Authentication | None (relies on process permissions) | **API key required** |
| Quota | None | **Yes** (the official docs mention "higher quotas") |
| Open-source licence | Reference implementation, no commercial form | MIT code + hosted service |

**This brings a completely different class of risk**:
for other servers the risk is "what can it touch of yours";
for Context7 the risk is "where do your queries go".

sections.正确用法（README 强调的三点）:
This is the most operationally valuable information:

| Point | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Use Library Id** | Query by library ID, not fuzzy names |
| **Specify a Version** | **Specify the version** — without it you get mismatched docs |
| **Add a Rule** | Declare a rule: always use Context7 when library docs are needed |

**"Specify a Version" matters most** —
stale model training data is the core problem this class of tool solves;
if you do not pin the version, you likely get docs for a newer version while the code behaves per the old one.
sections.认证方式与额度：三档，两处容易看错:
```
Manual config: use the server endpoint https://mcp.context7.com/mcp
and pass the key via the Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY header
```

Installers support an OAuth flow that generates the key automatically. The Free tier itself supports **OAuth 2.0**.

**Official wording**: API Key Recommended — get a free key for higher quotas.

### Quota tiers (verified against the official plans page, 2026-10-01)

(Price figures are not stored per our D9 rule — always see the official plans page; quotas are capability boundaries and are recorded as-is.)

| Tier | Included quota | After exceeding |
|---|---|---|
| **Free** | **1,000 calls/month** | Blocking (exact behaviour not stated officially) |
| **Pro** | **2,000 calls / seat** | **Does not block** (overage billed by usage; unit price on the official page) |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom |

**The two easiest misreadings**:

**① Pro's "Unlimited API Calls" does not mean "unlimited and free" — it means "does not block".**
The official comparison table writes Pro's Additional API Calls column as
"Unlimited (overage billed by usage)" — the first half means no blocking, the second half means overage costs extra.

**② Private Repo Parsing is a completely separate billing item.**
It is **a different wallet** from the API-call quota; the Pro seat price does not include it.
If you want private-library docs ingested, that cost is calculated separately (unit price on the official page).

### Third-party figures disagree with the official page (official prevails)

Several third-party sites (around 2026-09) claim Pro is "**5,000 calls/seat**" —
**the official page says 2,000**. This entry follows the official figure; the third-party number is treated as outdated or speculative.

### Draw the open-source boundary clearly

The official README itself states: **this repository hosts only the MCP server's source code;
the API backend, parsing engine and crawling engine are proprietary.**
So "MIT" refers to that client-side code, not the whole service.
sections.风险评估:
| Risk type | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Local file leakage | **None** — touches no local files |
| Internal-network probing | **None** — does not visit arbitrary URLs |
| **Data egress** | **Yes, but narrow in scope** — sends only **the documentation question + library name/ID**; not full prompts, source code or conversation history (official statement, see note below) |
| Credential risk | Low — one API key only, no file permissions; the official docs also require agents not to put credentials in queries |
| Service availability | Depends on the Upstash service; this repository's releases cannot guarantee service status |
| **Budget overrun** | **Yes** — behaviour after Free exceeds 1,000 calls/month is unknown; Pro does not block on overage but bills by usage; private-repo parsing is a separate billing item (unit price on the official page) |

**The part sensitive scenarios must assess**: if the library names, error messages or code snippets you query are themselves sensitive,
they leave your machine.

**But this round adds one explicit official privacy commitment** (the official FAQ has a dedicated entry,
"How do you keep the privacy of my queries?"):

Queries send only **the documentation question and the library name/ID**,
**not full prompts, source code or conversation history**;
the official docs also require agents not to carry credentials, personal data or proprietary code in queries.

⚠ This statement is the **vendor's own account**; this site has not verified it by measurement —
i.e. no packet capture confirmed the outbound content matches the description.
